title: The book he can't check out
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The college library has one book of Daumier lithographs. Auditors can't check books out. Wood reads it standing up in the stacks for an hour. The librarian brings him a stool.

panels.composition: The library stacks. WOOD standing with a heavy book open: lithographs, a fat king drawn as a pear. BARNABY not present — dogs, still.

image.prompt: a young man standing in library stacks holding a heavy open book of nineteenth-century lithographs, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The page: a king as a pear, a courtroom of jowls, a line that knows where it's going.

image.prompt: close on a page of old lithographs showing a corpulent king drawn as a pear and a courtroom of caricatured faces, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The LIBRARIAN's cardigan at the end of the aisle. A stool set down. Nothing said.

image.prompt: a librarian in a cardigan setting a wooden stool down at the end of a library aisle without a word, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood on the stool. The book on his knees. The stacks. An hour drawn as one panel.

image.prompt: a young man sitting on a stool in library stacks with a heavy book open on his knees, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Auditors can't check out. The stool. The librarian: a cardigan, again.
